title: Elodie and the Ledger
premise: Hazel Brightwater, the meticulous archivist of Saint Aldhelm's Cathedral, is hired to close the cold case of Elodie Vane, a parish ledger-keeper who vanished eleven years ago, leaving behind a locked crypt and a diary that ends mid-sentence. When a second diary surfaces in the crypt's sealed annex — its entries continuing for three years after her disappearance in Hazel's own handwriting style — he realizes Elodie lived on under another name, hiding from someone inside the cathedral itself. Following the ledgers' coded margins, Hazel uncovers a forged inheritance scheme that disinherited Elodie's ward, protected by the very canon who hired him. In the crypt at last light, Hazel finds the witness everyone swears is dead: Elodie herself, alive as the cathedral's night caretaker, who chose erasure over complicity. Together they expose the forgery, and Hazel learns that belonging sometimes means burning your own ledger.
about_author: Felix Zhou is a former parish records clerk turned novelist who writes mysteries about paper trails and the people they erase. He lives above a bookbindery in York, where he claims every locked door has a story attached.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Hazel Brightwater, POV. Canon Merrick hires Hazel to catalog the sealed crypt before a heritage inspection, dangling the unsolved disappearance of ledger-keeper Elodie Vane as bait for his pride. Hazel accepts against his better judgment. Emotional beat: quiet vanity masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Dust
chapters.summary: Hazel descends into the crypt and finds it undisturbed except for one chair moved recently. He catalogs Elodie's effects: her diary ending mid-sentence on the day she vanished. Emotional beat: the thrill of an impossible puzzle.

chapters.title: A Diary That Keeps Writing
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. At home he rereads the diary and discovers loose pages tucked in the binding — entries continuing three years past her disappearance, written in handwriting unnervingly like his own. Emotional beat: professional confidence cracking into unease.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Buried
chapters.summary: Hazel interviews the verger, Mrs. Okonkwo, who insists Elodie is dead — she attended the funeral. But there is no grave, no certificate, only a memorial plaque paid anonymously. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into certainty.

chapters.title: Margins and Codes
chapters.summary: Hazel studies the old parish ledgers and finds tiny marginal marks beside certain names — payments, substitutions, dates shifted by days. Someone was rewriting history in plain sight. Emotional beat: the archivist's joy curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Canon Merrick's Generosity
chapters.summary: Merrick pressures Hazel to finish quickly and dismisses the diary pages as a hoax. Hazel notices Merrick's name appears in the coded margins more than anyone's. Emotional beat: the client becoming the suspect.

chapters.title: Elodie's Ward
chapters.summary: Hazel tracks down Tomas Vane, Elodie's ward, now a struggling stonemason who was cut out of his family bequest the year she disappeared. He remembers her teaching him cipher games with ledger marks. Emotional beat: inherited loss, tender and raw.

chapters.title: The Second Chair
chapters.summary: Nighttime, Hazel stakes out the crypt and hears movement below — but finds only fresh candle wax and a folded note in the coded margin language: STOP COUNTING. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Funeral Hid
chapters.summary: Hazel locates the retired undertaker, who admits the coffin was sealed empty at Merrick's instruction; the death certificate bears a signature he's seen before — in the ledgers. Emotional beat: the dead weight of old bargains.

chapters.title: Handwriting
chapters.summary: A forensic document examiner tells Hazel the diary continuation isn't forged — it's the same hand as the original entries, just aged, hurried, changed. Elodie wrote both. She survived. Emotional beat: vertigo of a case reopening itself.

chapters.title: Tomas's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas reveals Elodie left him a child's practice ledger full of ciphers; decoded, it names 'the Canon' and a phrase: 'the inheritance must die with me.' Hazel realizes the scheme targeted Tomas all along. Emotional beat: protective anger.

chapters.title: The Annex
chapters.summary: Hazel finds the crypt's hidden annex behind a memorial panel — a furnished room, lived in within the last decade, with a second diary missing its final volume. Emotional beat: intimacy with a stranger's hiding place.

chapters.title: Mrs. Okonkwo Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted, the verger confesses she helped Elodie disappear after discovering Merrick's forgeries, then spent years believing Elodie had died abroad. Her certainty was loyalty, not knowledge. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into alliance.

chapters.title: Merrick Closes the Door
chapters.summary: Merrick suspends Hazel's commission, changes the crypt lock, and hints at Hazel's own precarious employment history. The message is clear: stop, or be erased too. Emotional beat: threat wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: The Missing Volume
chapters.summary: Hazel deduces the final diary volume would be where Elodie felt safest — the cathedral library's restricted shelf, misfiled under his own predecessor's name. Inside: her account of the forged will and a meeting place. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Night Caretaker
chapters.summary: Following the diary's instructions, Hazel waits in the cloister at matins hour and sees her: a gray, stooped woman lighting candles — Elodie Vane, alive, watching him back. Emotional beat: awe and heartbreak in one glance.

chapters.title: Why She Vanished
chapters.summary: Elodie's account, her voice: she caught Merrick forging the bequest that would have pauperized Tomas; exposed, she'd have been discredited and silenced, so she buried herself instead and guarded the evidence for eleven years. Emotional beat: sacrifice mistaken for cowardice.

chapters.title: The Price of Proof
chapters.summary: Elodie refuses to testify — exposure means prison for her false death and ruin for those who sheltered her. Hazel must find proof that convicts Merrick without destroying her. Emotional beat: ethics pulling against justice.

chapters.title: Counting Backward
chapters.summary: Hazel reconstructs the forgery from the ledgers' marginal codes plus the undertaker's testimony and the empty-coffin receipt signed in Merrick's hand. The chain is complete — if he can get it out of the building. Emotional beat: methodical hope.

chapters.title: Last Light in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Climax. Merrick corners Hazel in the crypt intending to seal it with him inside; Elodie and Tomas intervene, and the confrontation is witnessed by the arriving heritage inspectors Hazel secretly tipped off. Merrick is taken for questioning. Emotional beat: terror breaking into daylight.

chapters.title: Names Restored
chapters.summary: Resolution begins: the will is voided, Tomas inherits, and Elodie negotiates a plea that spares her allies. She chooses to keep her new name but reclaim her story publicly through the diaries, published with Hazel's editing. Emotional beat: identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Burning the Ledger
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Hazel's POV. Hazel closes the case file, declines Merrick's vacated post, and shares tea with Elodie in the annex, now a reading room. He understands belonging isn't being recorded — it's choosing who holds your record. Emotional beat: peace earned, doors unlocked.
